# #1575: Patch: a refused chosen action falls back to the AI's next-best line, not the generic fallback
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Once in a while the practice AI picks a play it turns out not to be allowed — a face-down trap quietly taxes its hand, so its sampled worlds said the play was fine but the real board refuses it. Today the AI then throws the plan away and ends its turn or takes the first legal thing; after this it takes its second-best plan instead, so one hidden tax stops wasting its whole turn.

## Why
`submitted()` in `crates/ai/src/decide.rs:517-554` trials the chosen action against the true state and, on refusal, walks `replacements_for` — endTurn, then a prompt answer, then any legal action — while the scored finalists it just computed sit unused. The comment names the case: a face-down aura trap taxes the hand the determinizations could not see (R403). The fix uses information the AI already produced: the runner-up first actions were scored across every determinization.

## Proposal
Keep the ordered finalist first-actions through to submit; on a refusal, trial each in order before falling back to `replacements_for`. Fallback semantics (`DecisionReason::Fallback`) stay for the true replacement path.

## Where it lands
`crates/ai/src/decide.rs` and its tests; spec §9.9.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test plants a hidden-cost refusal and asserts the submitted action is the runner-up line's first action, not endTurn
- [ ] `cargo jackioh gate` (smoke) still passes; no fallback-path games counted as decision failures beyond today's
- [ ] No config change needed — no new constants

## Size and risks
Small-medium; pure and seeded, one decision-boundary change in the AI.
